text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Differences within the left-wing Socialist People's Party over the Amsterdam EU Treaty do not mean a split in the party. If a national meeting votes against the treaty, supporters of the accord should resign the party's EU spokesman's post but can retain other senior positions.
--A.P.Moller is investing 200 million crowns in a new oil terminal in Oman and in taking over an oil and gas production concession there.
--Private and business customers borrowed more money, at lower rates, during the first half of 1997 than previously.
--Changes to welfare regulations mean that unemployed people turning down job offers will still receive benefits in more cases than previously.
--The Danish Bankers' Assocciation will discuss ethical guidelines at its August 12 board meeting.
--Investment company Options Invest Danmark is to close as the Financial Supervisory Authority has not given it approval.
--Cut-price British airline Debonair is to seek a listing on the European Easdaq exchange.
--The Danish Bacon and Meat Council estimates that pork export earnings will rise about two billion crowns to 23 billion this year compared to 1996.
